views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold our calibrated retaliation as leverage but pursue negotiation rather than further escalation. Keep the higher tariffs on ~$60B of US goods and the 'unreliable entity list' threat on the table, but use the upcoming leadership meeting to seek a truce — signaling willingness to renew purchase commitments to avoid Washington activating the full ~$300B across-the-board tariff. Do not escalate new measures that would hand the US an excuse to broaden the war into every sector.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to China is high, not existential. The US raised List 3 tariffs from 10% to 25% on ~$250B of Chinese goods (May 10), added Huawei and 70 affiliates to the Entity List (May 16) and saw Google and US chip suppliers cut Huawei off — a direct attack on our key tech champion and on Made-in-China-2025 self-sufficiency goals (timeline 2019-05-10, 2019-05-16, 2019-05-20; web: milli Huawei $105B business at stake, CNN 'dangerous new level'). Trump has ordered preparation of tariffs on the remaining ~$300B, which could hit late June (web: SCMP June 1). These map onto the +0.5 'major export sectors hit, firm-level targeting (Huawei)' anchor, with the Huawei decoupling and $300B threat warranting a reading a touch above, at +0.6. But China is not cornered: we have already invoked calibrated retaliation ($60B tariffs from June 1), announced an 'unreliable entity list' (May 31), and signaled rare-earth leverage (Xi's rare-earth facility visit, May 20) without deploying it — keeping escalation options in reserve (timeline). Crucially, the US is also under strain: the 10Y Treasury yield collapsed from ~2.9% in late 2018 to 2.12% by June 5 and Baa spreads tightened, and Trump still references wanting a deal. That mutual pain, plus the huge cost of a $300B tariff wave to our export economy, argues against escalating further (which would invite the full decoupling and tariff cascade) and against capitulating (which would forfeit our leverage). The optimum is a negotiated truce at the leadership level: maintain posture, hold firm on red lines (Huawei, structural reform), offer the purchases the US wants to buy peace, and let the pressure already evident in US markets work for us.
key_factors: US raised List 3 tariffs 10%→25% on ~$250B of Chinese goods (May 10)
Huawei +70 affiliates added to Entity List May 16; Google/chip suppliers cut ties — attack on China's tech champion and self-sufficiency
Trump ordered prep of ~$300B across-the-board tariffs, possible late June
China retaliated: higher tariffs on ~$60B US goods (June 1), 'unreliable entity list' (May 31), rare-earth signals retained as undepoloyed leverage
US also under strain: 10Y yield ~2.9%→2.12% by June 5, tightening Baa spreads — mutual pain favors negotiated de-escalation
Leadership meeting (G20) available as forum for a truce
